Communication at the service
of the Third Sector.

I put my marketing and visual communication skills at the service of an NGO working on European and international projects — creating concrete graphic materials that contributed to the organisation's fundraising and visibility.

Brand Identity · Design · Communication

Institutional brochure
and identity materials

I designed and produced the NGO's institutional brochure, taking care of every graphic and editorial aspect: from the choice of layout to the hierarchy of information, from tone of voice to institutional colours. The goal was to tell the organisation's mission, values and projects clearly and engagingly to a diverse audience — donors, institutional partners, European bodies.

I managed the graphic production of the materials first-hand, coordinating with management to ensure consistency with the association's visual identity. The result is a professional brochure ready to be distributed at institutional occasions, events and partner meetings.

Graphic products
for fundraising

I created graphic materials specifically for the organisation's fundraising campaigns: posters, flyers, digital content and materials to hand out at events. Every piece was designed to convey the urgency and value of the NGO's work, encouraging donations and community participation.

I worked on the visual storytelling of fundraising — using images, numbers and real stories to build empathy with the audience and motivate action. The materials were used in both physical and digital contexts.

EXPO Osaka 2025

The results I helped
to build.

EXPO Osaka 2025 — theme "Designing Future Society for Our Lives" — opened on 13 April 2025 and closed on 13 October 2025. As Social Media Assistant & Content Manager of the Italian Commissioner General's Office, I was part of the team that led the digital communication strategy from the inside: editorial planning, content production, media relations, data analysis, VIP management. These are the numbers that strategy generated — results that surpassed every previous record for an Italian presence at a world expo.

Preparatory phase · Social Strategy

Pre-EXPO: Myaku-Myaku
meets Italia-chan

courtesy of Italy Pavilion

In the run-up to the EXPO opening, I built a social strategy around identity-driven, potentially viral content: I worked on the narrative of Myaku-Myaku — the official mascot with a thousand eyes — meeting Italia-chan, the Italian character I helped promote on the Pavilion's official channels.

I produced the teaser content, video clips and coordinated posts across all channels, aiming to build a cultural bridge between the Japanese and Italian audiences. The project generated strong engagement from the weeks before the opening.

I also collaborated with other pavilions — including Heidi (Switzerland) — on cross-pavilion content with Italia-chan, broadening the visibility of the Italy brand.

Media Day: the press
gets in first

I organised and managed the Italy Pavilion's Media Day — exclusive access reserved for accredited Italian and international journalists before the official opening. A key event for building EXPO media coverage from day one.

I helped organise accreditations, guided tours, interview areas and the production of multilingual press kits (IT · EN · JP). I supported relations with the MAECI press office and contributed to live coverage on social channels. The result? 530 journalists met at the pavilion throughout EXPO.

Event Management · VIP Logistics

Opening, Closing &
Theme Days

▶️ Guarda: Opening Day — video ufficiale

Over the 184 days of EXPO, the Italy Pavilion hosted a series of major events with the general public, VIPs, institutional delegations and accredited press. Each event required separate planning, with different audiences, protocols and communication.

Opening Day (13 April 2025):the big opening day, with an official ceremony, ministerial delegations, national TV coverage and live social streams. Management of hospitality, ceremonial and real-time communication.

Theme days:every week the pavilion hosted dedicated days — fashion and design, Italian gastronomy, industry, sustainability, Italian regions. Each day required tailored content, targeted invitations and coordination with the day's partners.

Closing Day (13 October 2025):closing ceremony in collaboration withMilano Cortina 2026— a common thread with the next major international event — with a final summary, legacy video and international coverage.

Types of events managed

Opening Day and Closing Day with national TV coverage
Weekly theme days (fashion, food, tech, sustainability)
VIP and institutional events with diplomatic protocol
210+ business events with stakeholders and entrepreneurs
Site visits, briefings and pre-event logistics coordination
Live coverage and post-production for every event
How we invited and managed events
  • Teasing on social channels ahead of the event
  • Press cards and press releases
  • Ad hoc invitations via mailing lists, with reminders
  • Registration forms to track attendance and follow up on numbers
  • Managing visitor flow during the event
  • Organising interviews and live broadcasts

Entertainment · Audience Management

Italy Pop Music Fest:
Italian music in Osaka

courtesy of Italy Pavilion

I contributed to managing communications for the "Italy Pop Music Fest" concert series — one of the most iconic moments of the entire EXPO. I handled access logistics, audience management and all content production for the music events.

I prepared interviews and worked with artists such asLigabue, Achille Lauro e Negramaro, as well as coordinating with Japanese pop artists. I produced the teasers, video clips and live coverage posts for every concert.

The content produced for these events was among the best-performing of the entire EXPO: peaks of over 1M views per single post, with the Ligabue interview going viral.

Key activities

Access management and audience logistics for concerts (thousands of attendees)
Preparing and conducting artist interviews (e.g. the Ligabue interview — viral)
Production of teasers, short clips and recap videos for every event
Coordination with Italian and Japanese artist management
Live social coverage with peaks of 1M+ views per single piece of content

TV, web CMS
and Japanese media

I managed relations with Italian and Japanese TV broadcasters throughout EXPO, coordinating the Pavilion's presence on 172 Italian and 150 Japanese TV programmes.

National live TV broadcasts:I organised and logistically supported live broadcasts from our spaces for the main Italian broadcasters, bringing EXPO into Italian homes every week.

Yomiuri TV documentary:I worked with the historic Japanese broadcaster Yomiuri TV on the documentary about Italy at EXPO 2025 — I handled filming permits, editorial coordination and support for the Japanese journalistic team.

With the Yomiuri TV team during filming at the Italy Pavilion

Daily clips:every day I contributed to producing and publishing short videos on the activities and institutional visits to the pavilion — 184 days, 184 clips. A living archive of the Italian EXPO, built one piece of content at a time.

Official Italy website CMS — in collaboration with Almaviva:I managed the CMS of the Italy Pavilion's official website, working closely with Almaviva's technical team. I handled publishing and updating content: information pages, events, news and real-time updates. Constant editorial work that kept the site up to date for Italian and international visitors.

Official EXPO CMS — Italian pavilion:I managed the Italy Pavilion's presence on the CMS of the exposition's official platform, updating pavilion information, the events schedule and visitor guides. This channel was the main entry point for millions of visitors planning their EXPO visit — keeping content accurate and current was strategic to maximise traffic to the pavilion.

Institutions · Territory · Promotion

The Italian Regions
in Osaka: every week

Throughout EXPO, the team handled communications for every regional week — a rotation that brought a different Italian region to the Osaka stage each week. I contributed directly to this intense rhythm across all 184 days, adapting content each time.

For each region I produced dedicated content, coordinated with regional delegations and councils, created custom guides for visitors and organised promotional events. I also handled invitations to journalists and the local Japanese community, building an authentic narrative about Italian territory every week.

From Trentino-Alto Adige to Sicily, from Valle d'Aosta to Apulia: every region brought its own identity, products and talents to the world's biggest stage.

Activities for each regional week

Coordination with regional delegations and tourism and culture departments
Dedicated social content in IT, EN and JP
Custom guides for pavilion visitors
Promotional events (tastings, exhibitions, performances)
Invitations and communications to Japanese journalists and local communities
Feedback collection and weekly reporting for the Commissioner's Office

Regional and corporate events were also held in the Pavilion's Auditorium, in addition to the other exhibition spaces.

Post-EXPO · Legacy · Publishing

The Pavilion's Legacy:
museum and book

When EXPO closed on 13 October 2025, the team kept working on the legacy phase. I contributed actively to make sure everything we had built in six months would not be lost.

Legacy at the Osaka Museum:I took part in selecting and transferring the Italy Pavilion's works and installations to a museum in Osaka, where they will be on permanent display. A concrete cultural legacy of our team's work. (Source: ANSA)

Legacy book with Gangemi Editore:I contributed to the editorial curation of the volume dedicated to EXPO Osaka 2025, published by Gangemi Editore — a historic Italian publisher of art and architecture. The book gathers the projects, numbers and stories of a record-breaking edition — including those born from the communication strategy I helped build.

Key activities

Coordination of the donation and installation of works at the Osaka museum
Editorial curation of the legacy book with Gangemi Editore
Final content production: legacy video, recaps, EXPO highlights
Closing Day and institutional legacy communication
Digital archive of all content produced over the 184 days
